verdict: NO COURT WAS HELD - refutability scored 5/10, deliberately below the >=6 auto-escalate line, and the runner routed it to ADJUDICATE. The triage's own recommendation is explicit and mechanical: do not convene a court now, re-run the triage on 2026-08-14 with the Q2 balance sheet in hand, where it expects to score 7-8. This adjudication ratifies that routing. Like DGXX, the sector tag is an artifact - INV is tagged 'Finance / Blank Checks' but is an operating holdco whose value is essentially a consolidated AI-datacenter liquid-cooling subsidiary, Accelsius. The decisive analytical work is a reconstruction that resolves the loudest claim before the print. Management reaffirmed on the 2026-05-15 Q1 call that Accelsius exits December 2026 with positive operating cash flow at roughly a $100M revenue run rate, clarified as running at $8-9M of revenue per month by year end. Accelsius did $1.3M of revenue in Q1'26 (93% of the $1.4M consolidated), so reaching about $26M in Q4 requires roughly Q2 $4M, Q3 $11M, Q4 $26M - a 20x ramp in three quarters of physically shipped two-phase direct-to-chip hardware. Hardware revenue is preceded by a working-capital build, and on the 3/31/2026 balance sheet every line that must lead such a ramp moved the WRONG way: inventory $1,562k against $1,604k (down), contract liabilities $275k against $947k (-71%), accounts receivable $840k against $1,094k (down), and only $0.8M of Accelsius PP&E invested in the quarter. The triage states the blue-team outs fairly rather than burying them - management said larger customers probably will not pay deposits, which weakens deferred revenue as a tell for this mix, and a contract-manufacture or drop-ship model would suppress on-balance-sheet inventory - but correctly notes those do not cover three independent lines plus capex all moving together. The insight worth preserving is the identification of the right decisive line: it is NOT the Q2 revenue print, because a back-half-weighted ramp is consistent with a small Q2 - it is the 6/30/2026 inventory and contract-liability balances. If inventory is still around $2M on 8/13, the December run-rate target is dead on arrival regardless of call commentary. The second pre-print resolvable is the liquidity bridge, and it also fails management's framing: $55.4M unrestricted plus $5.0M restricted at 3/31 (the restricted amount is a WTI Facility covenant minimum), plus $11.9M drawn on the Yorkville SEPA after quarter-end, against -$34.0M of quarterly operating cash flow, implies roughly $33-39M unrestricted at 6/30 before further draws and roughly $5-15M by 9/30, against $19.8M of debt due within twelve months and $6M of 5.0% convertible debentures maturing 2026-09-15. Management's 'we do not anticipate the need to raise significant capital for the foreseeable future' fails on its own Q1 arithmetic inside about two quarters. The January raise cleared at $3.50 and the stock is $3.37 - below the last clearing price - with an open SEPA that sells into weakness, and share count went 55.2M to 80.1M in nine months (+45%). What is NOT dead, and the triage is careful about this, is that the subsidiary-level capital formation is real and non-toxic: Accelsius closed a $65M Series B led by Johnson Controls ($35M) and Legrand ($30M) in January 2026, revenue is genuinely accelerating (+600% YoY, up from $0.8M in Q4'25), and a 300MW NeuCool deployment agreement with DarkNX is signed. That is why the class is DAMAGE-ARRIVING rather than STRUCTURAL - the magnitude turns on whether strategic capital converts to shipped revenue or stays a pipeline.
